Bo French

Republican candidate for Railroad Commissioner, Texas

Investor; former chair of the Tarrant County Republican Party

Bo French is a Midland native whose family owns French Oil, a Midland-based oil company, and he is a former chair of the Tarrant County Republican Party. He challenged incumbent Railroad Commissioner Jim Wright in the March 3, 2026 Republican primary, finishing second (31.75% to 32.1%). He then defeated Wright in the May 26, 2026 runoff, about 50.7% to 49.3%, to win the Republican nomination.

Where French stands

Oil and gas regulation
Supports deregulating the oil and gas industry. Says the commission's job is to stay out of the way so the industry can produce more oil, which he says would strengthen Texas refining.
Energy prices
Promises to lower electricity and gas prices. Says Texas leaders' willingness to produce oil makes the difference at the pump.
Foreign ownership of energy assets
Proposes cracking down on foreign ownership of oil and gas wells, and has campaigned on Chinese-owned land.
DEI programs
Supports further cuts to diversity, equity and inclusion (DEI) programs.
Abortion
Says he will promote anti-abortion policies.
Immigration
Said in March 2026 that 100 million people should be deported from the U.S. Called the Supreme Court's June 2026 ruling upholding birthright citizenship traitorous.
Campaign priorities
After the runoff, said his campaign focused on defending oil and gas and putting America First.

Background

  • Former chair, Tarrant County Republican Party
  • Investor; family owns French Oil (Midland)
  • Native of Midland, Texas; age 56 (per Texas Tribune, Oct. 2026)
  • Announced run for Texas Railroad Commission, November 2025
  • Advanced to runoff in March 3, 2026 Republican primary (31.75%)
  • Won May 26, 2026 Republican primary runoff over incumbent Jim Wright (~50.7%)
